goldens.comment: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.
goldens.reasoning: C1 says the test asserts without joining the reader thread, so an in-flight failure after the assertion is missed. That is the same race the golden comment describes.

candidates: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:155 - Reader thread is never stopped or joined if deletion fails. If a `remove()` call throws, `deletedAll.set(true)` is skipped. The non-daemon reader thread then loops forever and can hang the test JVM. On the success path the test also asserts without joining the thread. A request still in flight can fail after the assertion, and that failure is missed. Wrap the deletes in try/finally that sets the flag. Keep a reference to the thread, join it before asserting, and consider making it a daemon.
